rule.description: A function defined in one module is dominated by the internal state of an encapsulated struct owned by a different module: at least 5 direct member accesses on one owner-mapped struct, at least 65% of the function's total member accesses, with the function living outside the struct's owner module.

checks.description: Detect functions whose member-access interest is dominated by a struct owned by another module (kernel writer state, kernel reader state, or symbol table state owned by utils/kernel.c / utils/symbol.c) while being defined outside that owner module.
checks.detected_relation: consumer-module function -> foreign owner-module encapsulated struct state
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The function's data interest is concentrated on a struct whose owning module already maintains all of that struct's other manipulation; the consumer module reaches around the owner and manipulates its internals directly, so the owner-side lifecycle is fragmented or withered.

matches.evidence: Constructs the kernel writer's per-cpu state (cpu count, traces/fds arrays, -1 initialization) inside the record command instead of inside the kernel module's writer setup where it used to live.
Opens the kernel writer's per-cpu tracefs trace pipes and kernel-cpu output files inside the record command; the kernel module's start function only toggles tracing afterwards.
Drains, closes and frees the kernel writer's per-cpu trace state in the record command's finish path; the kernel module's finish function keeps only the saving/reset half.

Constructs the whole kernel reader (parser init, kernel-cpu directory scan, header loading, per-cpu rstack state) inside the data-file layer instead of the kernel module; needed a public-header exposure of the header loader to compile.
Tears down the kernel reader's per-cpu rstack/parser state and frees its per-cpu arrays inside the data-file layer instead of the kernel module.

A command-local copy of the symbol module's by-name probe (with its own comparator) iterates each module's symbol table for depth-trigger synthesis, while the symbol module's own probe remains for its other callers.

excluded.description: Per-task reader state (struct uftrace_task_reader and its fstack), session/task trees, the options bundle, trigger data, report/graph node trees, ELF/module descriptors, perf reader state and the per-record struct uftrace_record are deliberately unmapped: they are shared data models consumed from anywhere by design, so access concentration on them does not indicate feature envy here.
Functions defined in the owner module itself never match (module identity equals owner identity), e.g. utils/kernel.c read_kernel_cpu_data (7/9 on uftrace_kernel_reader) is not a match.

Address-lookup compositions in cmds/replay.c, utils/session.c and utils/fstack.c split their member-access interest across struct uftrace_mmap, struct uftrace_sym_info, struct uftrace_module and the task reader state; no single owner-mapped struct approaches the share threshold, so they are not matches.
libmcount/* translation units belong to the injected runtime loaded into traced processes and are outside the main-binary analysis scope of this case's checker.
